newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products mostly weaker after bearish APIs.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products mostly weaker after bearish APIs.

text.p: NWE oil products were mostly weaker across the barrel on Wednesday, traders said.
Weaker crude and Tuesday's API report for U.S. oil stocks, showing a surprisingly bearish decline in demand for gasoline and distillates fuelled weaker sentiment for much of the barrel.
The thinly talked naphtha spot market showed less of a reaction but offers for well supplied prompt cargoes slipped $2-3 to around $183 off around $3.50 from the previous trade.
Both spot and paper gasoline were hit with prompt Amsterdam/Rotterdam lifting barges trading some $2-3 lower at $190.50 a tonne and May swaps $1-2 down at $194.75/$195.25.
Gas oil was knocked about $2 lower as the APIs hit futures, but barge and cargo premiums held broadly steady.
High sulphur fuel oil was steady, ignoring futures, with prompt barges trading at $82.50, but low sulphur prices were knocked down on futures and poor demand to a notional $86/$87 fob.
